outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Current Landscape of RLHF in Large Language Models
outline.description: An introduction to Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) in the context of scaling language models, establishing the necessity of stable training dynamics, and reviewing the standard architectures used (Dense and Mixture-of-Experts).
subtopics: Overview of RLHF: From Supervised Fine-Tuning to PPO
The Human Verifier: Scoring responses and preference learning
Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO): A Quick Primer
The Stability Crisis: Model Collapse and Catastrophic Failure
The MoE Challenge: Why Sparsity Breaks Standard RL Algorithms

outline.description: A rigorous development of the mathematical theory behind Group Sequence Policy Optimization, contrasting the theoretical correctness of sequence-level importance sampling against the flawed token-level approach.
subtopics: Probabilistic Language Modeling: Likelihoods and Autoregressive Generation
Principles of Importance Sampling: Why Token-Level Weights Fail
Deriving the Optimal Unit for Sequential Reward Alignment

outline.description: A detailed walkthrough of the GSPO implementation, focusing on how it replaces GRPO's components with sequence-level alternatives, including clipping, advantage estimation, and gradient flow.
subtopics: The GSPO Objective Function: Equation Review and Interpretation
Group-Based Advantage Estimation without Value Models
Deriving the GSPO Gradient Update Rule
Technical Equivalence: GSPO-token as a Flexible Variant

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 4: Stability, Efficiency, and Inference Integration
outline.description: An analysis of why GSPO converges faster and more stably than GRPO, featuring a deep dive into hardware utilization (batch size partitioning), memory efficiency, and compatibility with inference engines.
subtopics: # Counter-Intuitive Clipping Efficiency: Larger Failsures Mean Better Signals
# Noise Reduction in Long-Response Training Scenarios
# Integration with Training Engines vs. Inference Engines (Precision Matching)
# Advantages in Partial Rollouts and Multi-Turn Dialogues
